historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly prevents agent-driven physical input but collapses the test to a generic button observation and misses the mutually different target and IP oracles.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly preserves both branches and requires a ruling before the disruptive action while retaining a hybrid agent monitoring role.
historical_reviews.history: Exact-code/source search found no earlier V3.1 record for this identity.
historical_reviews.v3_1: A system reset normally interrupts host execution and OS-IP while a BMC reset interrupts the management controller and BMC-IP; the other plane may remain alive. Because those signatures are observably different, collecting both ping streams cannot repair an undefined authoritative target after the button has been pressed.

original_test_intent: Preserve the stated System Reset/OS-IP procedure while flagging the conflicting BMC Reset/BMC-IP criteria: validate the owner-approved physical reset button, its intended outage domain and recovery timeline.
original_method: Obtain a written owner ruling on system versus BMC reset and the exact physical control, drain affected workloads, establish independent OS-IP and BMC-IP observers plus console/LED/log baselines, have an authorized operator press the approved button once, record both planes through the approved recovery window, and stop without retry on unexpected scope or failed recovery.
manual_activity: The platform owner resolves the system-reset versus BMC-reset conflict and approves the exact button, outage/recovery oracle and maintenance plan; an authorized operator presses the physical control once.
required_inputs: Exact physical button and panel location
Expected host and BMC reset domains
Approved 10-15 minute or replacement recovery deadline
safety_requirements: Do not execute before the semantic ruling
Drain workloads and preserve uncommitted data
Require explicit approval for the disruptive reset
Agent must not press hardware or substitute an API reset
Do not power-cycle or issue a second reset to force recovery
Stop on wrong outage domain, boot loop or timeout
Preserve both management and host evidence
agent_execution_scope: Collect baseline OS/BMC reachability and health
Monitor both IPs, console and logs with synchronized timestamps
Correlate the operator-announced single button press
engineer_actions: Resolve reset target and source conflict
Approve exact button and dual-plane oracle
Authorize workload drain and physical reset
Perform or supervise one button press

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The physical-only NO correctly limits agent handling but omits the automatable dual-plane timeline and does not reveal that source procedure and criteria name different buttons, reset domains and IP targets.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After the owner ruling, have an authorized operator press the exact approved button once while the agent records synchronized OS-IP, BMC-IP, console, LED and preserved log evidence through recovery.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The 15-minute activity and procedure's 10-15 minute recovery expectation are preserved pending owner disposition of the conflicting BMC criteria.

modernized_recommendation.status: OWNER-RESOLVED PHYSICAL RESET WITH DUAL-PLANE TIMELINE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a state matrix for host, OS-IP, BMC-IP, console and LEDs before, during and after the single physical press, keyed to the approved reset type and deadlines.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds an authoritative target ruling, workload safety and independent host/BMC evidence instead of a generic visual observation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A BMC outage can leave the host running, while a host reset can leave the BMC reachable; checking the wrong IP would falsely validate the other reset path.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The physical stimulus is not automatable, and no monitoring sophistication can determine which mutually inconsistent source branch was intended without an owner decision.

project_override_considerations: Project must declare whether this row is System Reset or BMC Reset, the exact button, expected OS/BMC reachability matrix, LED/console signatures, recovery deadline and whether the conflicting branch is a copied criterion or separate testcase.
expected_evidence: Written source-conflict ruling and approved procedure revision
SUT/BMC/firmware/OS identity, IPs and workload-drain approval
Operator/button photographs and synchronized press timestamp
Console/LED/health and complete preserved log evidence
Recovery duration, no-repeat/no-substitution audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items and Procedure specify a physical System Reset button, OS-IP loss and whole-system recovery, while Criteria specify a BMC Reset button, BMC-IP loss and BMC recovery. These are different physical controls and outage domains and cannot be silently merged.

blocked_analysis.analysis: An authoritative owner ruling, button map and reachability oracle are obtainable inputs, so the review remains REQUIRES. Actual execution is blocked until that ruling is recorded.

engineering_decision_request.question: Resolve Functionality row 1741: whether the authoritative target is the System Reset button with OS-IP outage and whole-system recovery as stated by Items/Procedure, the BMC Reset button with BMC-IP outage/recovery as stated by Criteria, or separately accepted checkpoints; define the exact physical control, expected host/BMC reachability matrix, LED/console signature and recovery deadline while preserving Master.

review_improvement: Prevents a critical physical reset from being run against one control while judged with the other control's outage oracle.
independent_technical_reasoning: Host and management-controller resets have different failure containment: a system reset may drop OS networking but preserve BMC reachability, whereas a BMC reset may drop management networking while host workloads continue. Therefore button identity and the expected dual-plane matrix are part of the test purpose, not parameters that can be guessed after observing an outage.
